paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: everything hangs on one fact. Paul says if Christ has not been raised, "your faith is futile; you are still in your sins" (1 Corinthians 15:17). But that's the "if," and it doesn't get the last word. "But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep" (1 Corinthians 15:20), so your faith stands on SOLID ground!

And that word firstfruits is a promise, baker. Christ is the first, and those who belong to Him come next, each in his own turn (1 Corinthians 15:23). Death came through a man, and the resurrection of the dead comes through a man, so as in Adam all die, in Christ all will be made alive (1 Corinthians 15:21-22). Even death, the last enemy, will be destroyed (1 Corinthians 15:26). That's why I keep my ovens ready, friend, though I never know the day (Matthew 24:36).

So what do you do with that today? Paul says to "Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning" (1 Corinthians 15:34), because a hope that reaches past this life changes how you live right now. You don't have to live like "tomorrow we die" (1 Corinthians 15:32), and your labor in the Lord is never wasted. Hold on to the risen Christ, baker, and let that hope shape your whole day.
